claims.text: ADR 0031 decision: a separate reporting database on a server of its own (assumed); every hour (assumed) a job reads donhang, donhang_payments and every database the ADR 0026 shop map lists, and writes totals per shop per day (Vietnam time).
Nothing is built at stage-4: ADR 0031 notes there is no reporting database or job in the repository.
The shop map is a column of the shops table, owned by Ordering, in donhang; it records the database holding each shop's data, donhang by default. Only donhang moves shops out.
An ordinary PostgreSQL query reads only the database its connection opened; a query naming a table in another database fails with an error that cross-database references are not implemented.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 22.1 Overview (Managing Databases) — a connection can access only the database named in the request; error text from the parser on db.schema.table

claims.text: Each job run reads the last 3 days (assumed), about 150,000 orders on normal days, with short queries; its load on the sources is small compared with order placement.
Report queries read only the reporting database, so long report queries take no connection of the primary.

Every summary row carries a shop id; staff read by the shop taken from the access token (from release 2), with row-level security as ADR 0013 (assumed), which keeps every shop in shared tables; Đơn Hàng's team reads every row.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0031 @ stage-4 lines 43-44; ADR 0013 title and Quyết định; reporting-design-review.md lines 46-48

claims.text: The job reads each database and combines the results itself, with no query joining two databases; this answers the multi-shop review's open question on reports across all shops.

Rejected: reports on the primary (hold connections ordering needs, still no join); on db-replica (no primary connection, but a copy of the whole db server, no join across two databases, no moved shop's database); read model from messages (OrderMessage has no amounts or items).
db/replica/start.sh copies the whole db server with pg_basebackup and runs it as a streaming standby; the replica is behind db by its replication lag.
claims.source_hint: db/replica/start.sh @ stage-4 lines 5-18; PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_basebackup (backs up the whole cluster), 26.2 Log-Shipping Standby Servers

claims.text: OrderMessage (DonHang.Domain/OrderMessage.cs) has exactly four fields: OrderId, CustomerEmail, CustomerName, OccurredAt; no amount and no line items.
Adding amounts and items to order messages is a schema change every reader must accept, and orders placed before the change cannot be read again from the broker.
Each run recomputes the last 3 days (assumed) and replaces those days' rows, so a repeated run gives the same result; a hand edit to today's total is replaced by the computed figure on the next run.

Deep dive: the job reads the ADR 0026 shop map every run with no fixed list; a shop moved between runs is read from its new database next run; it is not counted twice since old rows are deleted only after a check period and the job reads one place per the map.

Consequences: figures up to one hour old plus the run time; one more database, server and job, owned by the Shop team (assumed); a new question such as sales per hour needs a new summary filled again from the sources.
The requirements accept figures up to two hours old (assumed), each shown with its as-of time; a failed job leaves figures getting older, each report still showing its as-of time.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/reporting-requirements.md @ stage-4 BC-1; ADR 0031 line 15; reporting-design-review.md line 70

claims.text: ADR 0031 ends with its revisit conditions: a requirement for live figures (order messages must then carry amounts); questions daily totals cannot answer in time, needing a store dedicated to analytical queries on detailed data.
Report amounts are copies; the owner of each figure stays Ordering or Payments, as data-ownership.md assigns.
When every report reads one database and no shop has moved, both reasons ADR 0031 gives against db-replica no longer apply, and the team would have to weigh it again against the drivers.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0031 lines 23-25 and 64-66 (replica rejected only for the join and moved shops)

claims.text: ADR 0031 does not state how the job will be scheduled.
A report query holds a connection far longer than placing an order: seconds against milliseconds (assumed).

Moving a shop (multi-shop review deep dive): its writes pause, its rows are copied to the new database and counted on both sides, then the map is switched; old rows in donhang are deleted only after a check period (assumed one week).
